source: docs/L7V2_DESIGN.md section 10 (the rule arms, their grids, the budget, the tau grid, R*), 9.1 and 9.5 (one policy, score(batch) -> p, rules give p in {0, 1}) and 8.3 (the population-level detector); ml/l7_baselines.py's grids; control_plane.py's default and tolerant heuristic; nginx.conf's limit_req
rule: Re-registered 2026-11-01 under the user's decision D-043 ('Benign quantiles'; 'M2; charge users behind'), post hoc but before any capture and before the code that reads it: it replaces ml/l7v2_rules_prereg_v2.json (format 2, T042-E08), whose level and decision points it keeps. Each rule is defined, tuned and decided at its own level as section 10 states it, on the validation captures only, at the common budget of ml/l7v2_model_prereg.json selection (budget, objective, ties, k_grid, theta_grid for the age-only arm) with the unit rule below; R* is chosen among best_rule.candidates of the verdict pre-registration. A change is a new file version, labelled post hoc; tests/test_l7v2_rules_prereg_v3.py pins the sha256 and every value.
label: re-registered 2026-11-01 under D-043, post hoc but before any capture

level.key_note: every per-key rule is keyed (IP, UA), as section 10 writes for the sustained rate and the token bucket; the cost budget's and the multi-scale rate's 'per key' is read the same way: a 32-token window of a C2 key spans seconds and sid rotation splits an (IP, UA) key, so neither the L7 v2 key nor its view windows are a rule's level
level.address: the population detector and the daemon heuristic act on the address; their per-request statistics are computed on the address's state and reach a key through its own requests
level.own: nginx's limit_req is per address, and it rejects a request: a key is acted on when one of its own requests is rejected

decision_points.rule: one row per (IP, UA) key and engine poll in which the key has at least one request: polls at whole multiples of poll_s of the log clock (a request completing at t belongs to the first poll after it, as train_l7v2.engine_scored), or the recording's own poll ticks in the replay (a request belongs to the first tick after its arrival)
decision_points.row: each statistic's maximum over the key's requests in the poll, so no request between two polls is lost
decision_points.time: a row's time is the completion of the key's last request in the poll; time to decision runs from the entity's first request start to it, as for the view arms
decision_points.policy: p > theta in k consecutive rows of the key (design 9.1), theta 0.5 for a rule; a suppressing poll (flood) clears every key's run and decides nothing, as the engine does
decision_points.entity: a key belongs to the entity of its first labelled request

statistic.time: a request's completion time (nginx $msec), clamped to be non-decreasing per state; requests are processed in (completion time, arrival) order within a poll
statistic.per_request: each statistic is computed at every request over its state's requests up to and including it (a live limiter's view), over wall-clock windows, with no cap on the history a window reaches

key.age: the time since the (IP, UA) key's first request

columns.rate: requests of the key completed in (T - w, T], divided by w (requests per second)
columns.cost: the sum, over the key's requests completed in (T - w, T], of the frozen class cost (ms) of each request's route class (route_costs_ms of the calibration record in use; an uncosted request costs 0)
columns.bucket: the token bucket's excess as ml/l7_baselines._bucket_rejects computes it: 0 at the key's first request, then max(0, excess - rate x dt + 1)
columns.ip_age: the time since the address's first request (descriptive: its validation AUC is reported, T042-F01)

unit_rule: a flagged (IP, UA) key costs every benign user behind it, because a deny there hits them all (D-043, E-4): the devices of its entity's plan that carry that UA (the plan user's 'device', one device per plan user without sessions, ml/l7_benign.session_users), and where the manifest has no plan for the entity, the key's distinct session ids; an entity's flagged units are at most its units. D-031's per-key rule (one unit per flagged key) stays for the view-level keys of the learned arms

sustained_rate.source: ml/l7_baselines.py SUSTAIN_WINDOWS, SUSTAIN_THRESHOLDS (B2), extended below 1 req/s (D-043)

token_bucket.source: ml/l7_baselines.py BUCKET_RATES, BUCKET_BURSTS (B3), rates extended below 1 req/s (D-043)

cost_budget.fires: cost over the window > its threshold level

multiscale_rate.fires: the rate over any of the windows > that window's threshold level

population.fires: either statistic of the key's address > its threshold level
population.pop_new_keys_60: the distinct L7 v2 keys (IP, UA, sid) first seen at the address in the last 60 s (a key unseen for lookback_s counts as new again)
population.pop_cookieless_60: the share of the address's requests in the last 60 s without a session id (sid_h = -1)

default_rules.rule: control_plane.py's L7 heuristic per address: requests kept for HEURISTIC_WINDOW s, at >= HEURISTIC_MIN_REQUESTS of them rps = n / max(elapsed, 1) > HEURISTIC_MAX_RPS, or error share > HEURISTIC_ERROR_RATIO with rps > 10 (status >= 400 except 503); a firing clears the address's tracker and bans it for BAN_TTL_SECONDS, during which its requests are not seen; the statistic is 1 while the address is banned

tolerant_rules.rule: as default_rules with control_plane.py's tolerant HEURISTIC_MAX_RPS

nginx_limits.rule: nginx.conf's limit_req per $binary_remote_addr, nodelay: a request whose excess would pass the burst is rejected and leaves the state unchanged. limit_conn is not replayable from the access log and is left out

age_only.score: p = the share of the benign validation rows whose (IP, UA) key age is greater (ties count one half), so a younger key scores higher and the theta grid reads quantiles of the benign ages
age_only.operating_point: theta_grid x k_grid of ml/l7v2_model_prereg.json selection, at the same budget and ties
age_only.use: a diagnostic beside the rule arms on validation (T042-F01: the role-coded lifetime moved to the address and the (IP, UA) key); its validation AUC (attack rows against benign rows) and its recall at the budget are reported beside every rule arm's recall; never R*, never live

selection: per tuned arm, the grid point and k with the highest validation attack-entity recall among those within the budget; ties: fewer benign units flagged, the lower median time to decision, then grid order (k in k_grid order, then the arm's grid in its grid_order, each dimension in its listed order). The fixed replays take their rule at k = 1 and are reported with their validation benign units, never selected
r_star_live: R* runs live on its own (IP, UA) path, beside the view engine: every log record feeds its statistics, every poll gives its rows, and the section-9 policy applies unchanged (p > 0.5 in k consecutive rows; flood suppression; the 20 s key-age gate and the allowlist; the graduated response, with a level-1 deny that covers every session of the (IP, UA) key and a level-2 ban only for a single-key address; rate caps and the kill switch); the replay scorer runs the same path
costs: the cost columns use the route costs of the calibration record in use; a rule package records the record's sha256 and its costs, and a selection is valid for claims only on a frozen record

threshold_levels.label: D-043, E-1: benign validation quantiles (median up to the maximum) beside section 10's multiples
threshold_levels.multiple_rule: a threshold is tau x the maximum of its statistic over the benign rows of the validation captures (design 10); a maximum of 0 gives the threshold 0
threshold_levels.quantile_rule: a threshold is the quantile (numpy's default, linear) of the statistic's per-key maximum over the benign (IP, UA) keys of the validation captures: at k = 1 a key is flagged on its maximum, so these levels read the share of benign keys flagged; the maximum itself is the multiple 1.0
threshold_levels.order: the multiples as listed, then the quantiles as listed
